title: 'It's kind of a unicorn,' 3.36-carat diamond found at Crater of Diamonds State Park - NewsBreak
text: MURFREESBORO, Ark. – A couple from Tampa, Florida, struck it rich at the Crater of Diamonds on July 1, uncovering a white 3.36-carat diamond. Cyndi and Gary Lovejoy were overjoyed when Scott and Jennifer Freitas returned with one of their rented kits and the gem. “It’s kind of a unicorn. It’s that mythical thing that you’re never going to find. They were expecting to just go out there and get dirty and muddy and have a good time, but they went home with what we call a legacy diamond,” Cyndi said. Lovejoy Diamond Screens posted pictures to social media after the couple returned their rented equipment. Cyndi used to work as a manager at the Crater of Diamonds Visitor Center before she and her husband opened their own business during the coronavirus pandemic. She explained diamonds are a rare treasure, even at the only place in America where the public can search and declare finders keepers. “The numbers work out to one out of every 250 to 300 people find a diamond. Averages to one or two a day,” Cyndi explained. According to the Lovejoys, Scott and Jennifer Freitas were on a road trip vacation to knock things off their bucket list, and this is likely the only one that required a bucket. They told the Lovejoys it only took three buckets before they came away with the stunning discovery. Those looking to make the most out of the trip will have buckets, shovels, boxes, a wagon, and even shade. Gary Lovejoy makes the sifting boxes that they rent and sell. He said the shift of emotions anytime people come back lucky is priceless. “I just love seeing and feeling the excitement when they come back saying, ‘Look what we found!’ I couldn’t ask for anything better,” Gary said. Cyndi stated the average size of a diamond found at the crater is about the size of a match head, or 15 times smaller than the one found Tuesday. The park should release more findings on the diamond’s quality in a week or so, but Lovejoy said she believes the diamond is easily worth at least $9,000 or $10,000 “They are excited. We’re excited. The whole town gets excited. The whole state gets excited, and this little bitty town trends in international news,” Cyndi stated. The Crater of Diamonds State Park is open every day from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to KLRT - FOX16.com.
